history.summary: Hilltop Devi temple on a ~1,600-foot hill at Dongargarh, revered as Badi Bamleshwari; a smaller Chhoti Bamleshwari shrine stands at the base of the hill about 1/2 km from the main complex. Local legend holds that the childless King Veersen performed puja to Shiva and Parvati and, blessed with a son, built the temple; another tradition links it to Maa Bagalamukhi appearing to King Vikramaditya. The temple is a major Shakti pilgrimage site drawing lakhs of devotees, especially during the Navratris of Kavar (Dusshera) and Chaitra (Ram Navami), with a tradition of lighting Jyoti Kalash during Navratri; the temple stays open 24 hours during Navratri. A ropeway (Udan Khatola) - the only passenger ropeway in Chhattisgarh - connects the base to the hilltop; devotees can also climb roughly 1,000 steps. A 2016 ropeway accident killed several people. CSV town corrected: the CSV gives 'Rajnandgaon', but the temple is in Dongargarh town, ~35-40 km from Rajnandgaon.

name: Maa Bamleshwari Temple, Dongargarh
town_description: Dongargarh is a city and municipality in Rajnandgaon district, about 35-40 km west of Rajnandgaon and around 100-130 km from Raipur. Its name derives from 'dongar' (mountain) and 'garh' (fort), and it is set among hills and ponds. Best known for the Bamleshwari hilltop temple and Chhattisgarh's only passenger ropeway, it is noted locally for religious harmony among Hindus, Buddhists, Sikhs, Christians and Jains.

travel.road: Via NH-6/NH-53; ~35-40 km from Rajnandgaon, ~100-140 km from Raipur
